steps.title: Spin down Texas Red tube
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Texas Red kit tube briefly so that any pellet settles at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Prepare 10X Texas Red stock
steps.instruction: Resuspend the Texas Red dye powder in 1 mL of 1X PBS to obtain a 10X stock (20 µM). After resuspension, pipette up and down and inspect the tip; if any particulates are visible, continue mixing until the solution is clear.

steps.title: Dilute to 1X working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the 10X stock with 1X PBS to make a 1X working solution (10 µM). Example: mix 100 µL of 10X stock with 900 µL of 1X PBS.

steps.title: Set up plate with PBS and reference
steps.instruction: Place the 96‑well plate on the bench. Add 100 µL of 1X PBS to every well in columns 2 through 12 (rows A‑D). Add 200 µL of the 1X Texas Red working solution to the wells in column 1 (rows A‑D). Column 12 will contain PBS only.

steps.title: Perform serial dilution across columns
steps.instruction: For each row (A, B, C, D) carry out a 10‑step serial dilution from column 1 to column 11:

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL from the column 1 well to the column 2 well.
Mix the column 2 well by pipetting up and down three times.
Transfer 100 µL from column 2 to column 3, mix 3×, and continue this pattern through column 11.
After mixing column 11, transfer the remaining 100 µL to liquid waste (do not continue into column 12).
Repeat the entire sequence for rows B, C, and D.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Place the plate in the plate reader. Measure fluorescence of all wells with the appropriate excitation and emission settings for red fluorescence. Ensure any automatic gain control is turned off. If you will also record OD, use the same instrument settings for both protocols and consider measuring OD at 660 nm (instead of 600 nm) when the red fluorescent protein absorbs at 600 nm.

steps.title: Record fluorescence data
steps.instruction: Write the fluorescence values and the gain setting (if displayed) in your lab notebook. Note that a few saturated points will not invalidate the standard curve.

steps.title: Import data into Excel
steps.instruction: Open the provided spreadsheet (iGEM 2019 Plate Reader Fluorescence Calibration v3_Texas Red.xlsx) and import the recorded data into the “Texas Red standard curve” tab.

steps.title: Optional: Verify stock concentration
steps.instruction: If a spectrophotometer is available, determine the exact concentration of the 10X Texas Red stock using the Beer‑Lambert law and record the value.

steps.title: Update spreadsheet concentration
steps.instruction: Enter the measured concentration into cell B1 of the “Texas Red Std curve” sheet; the rest of the spreadsheet will update automatically.
